lines.text: "title": "feat(host-control): Deck Apps ship their own host plugin as a .vdplugin package",

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: Eval: add vitadeck-144, a case for misses from unread files
lines.text:
"body": "Follow-up to #144, stacked on its branch. From an external author's or user's side, Host Control Plugins were clunky:
- a custom plugin meant an npm package of its own;
- a globally installed companion couldn't load a plugin installed somewhere else;
- the CLI was only `pnpm --dir js host-companion`.

The compromise is built-in plugins first, plus a package, like the Deck App's, for each Deck App's own plugin:

- **Built-ins.** Every companion now has `core` and `systemStats`. Deck Apps import the definitions from `@vitadeck/sdk/host-control`, together with `implementHostPlugin` and `HostCommandError`. `js/host-plugins/` is gone. Keys, media and opening apps are the next built-ins, but each one acts on the computer, so they wait for the credentials decision (ADR 0004).
- **A custom plugin lives in the Deck App's repo.**
  - `vitadeck create my-app --host-plugin` scaffolds `host/plugin.ts` (the commands) and `host/companion.ts` (the implementation).
  - `"hostPlugin": { "entry", "files"? }` in `vitadeck.config.json` makes `vitadeck build` and `vitadeck dev` also write a `dist/my-app.vdplugin/` package and a `dist/my-app.vdplugin.zip` archive. The package holds `manifest.json`, `companion.mjs` (the implementation with its npm dependencies bundled in) and an optional `files/` folder.
  - It's a package rather than one file because plugins will carry more than code: scripts, data, binaries. The entry reads them through `import.meta.url`.
- **Users install the archive:** `vitadeck-host-companion install my-app.vdplugin.zip` / `remove my-app`. A running companion reloads its plugins folder and any `--plugin` package or folder when they change, so the author's loop is `pnpm host` (`--plugin ./dist`) plus `vitadeck dev`, with no restarts.
- **Two CLIs, one per machine role.** `vitadeck` builds Deck Apps and plugin files; `vitadeck-host-companion` runs on any computer a Vita controls.
  - I didn't fold the companion into `vitadeck host`: a second command in the SDK package would break `npx @vitadeck/sdk`, and users shouldn't need Babel and rolldown just to run a server.
  - The companion is bundled into a single file with no dependencies. It stays `private: true` until a release.
  - The Shell's link hint now names `vitadeck-host-companion`.

ADR 0004, CONTEXT.md (new term: **Host Plugin Package**), AGENTS.md and the SDK, companion and demo READMEs are updated in place.

## Proof

- `scripts/agent-check.sh full` passed on 148fceef: JS checks, CTest, Docker smoke and the Vita VPK. Later commits change only JS: review fixes and the package format. On the head, `tsc`, lint, SDK tests (36) and companion tests (30) pass, and CI runs build, smoke and the Vita build.
- New tests:
  - `create --host-plugin` gives a project that passes `tsc` for both the app and `host/`, builds the package and zip with a self-contained entry, and whose `greet` command runs.
  - `hostPlugin.files` lands in `files/`, and a missing entry fails the build.
  - A package's entry reads its own `files/` through `import.meta.url`.
  - The companion CLI end to end: `install` of a `.vdplugin.zip` loads into a running companion, and `remove` unloads it. In a `--plugin ./dist` folder, a rebuilt package reloads and a broken rebuild keeps the previous one. `install` refuses built-in ids and anything but an archive or package.
  - Malformed manifests, entries outside the package, and zips with several roots or `../` paths are refused.
  - A bundled CommonJS dependency loads, because the entry is imported by file URL.
- I ran it as an external user in the macOS host window: [screenshots](https://matemolnar8.github.io/vitadeck/site/host-plugin-screenshots/).
  - I packed both packages, installed the companion globally into a temp prefix (it adds one package), and scaffolded `lights` outside the repo.
  - Install of the `.vdplugin.zip`, link and Greet worked, with Greet's reply including text the plugin read from its packaged `files/motd.txt`.
  - Editing the plugin and rebuilding changed the answer live; after `remove`, the app showed `unknown_plugin`.

## How to test

Run these from the repo root on the host build; they use your real `~/.vitadeck/`.

1. Set up:
   ```sh
   pnpm --dir js install && cmake --preset default && ninja -C out run
   ```
2. In a second terminal, pack both packages and act as an external user:
   ```sh
   pnpm --dir js build && mkdir -p /tmp/vdp
   pnpm --dir js --filter @vitadeck/sdk --filter @vitadeck/host-companion pack --pack-destination /tmp/vdp
   npm i -g --prefix /tmp/vdp/global /tmp/vdp/vitadeck-sdk-0.5.0.tgz /tmp/vdp/vitadeck-host-companion-0.1.0.tgz
   export PATH=/tmp/vdp/global/bin:$PATH
   cd /tmp/vdp && vitadeck create lights --host-plugin && cd lights
   npm pkg set "dependencies.@vitadeck/sdk=file:../vitadeck-sdk-0.5.0.tgz" "devDependencies.@vitadeck/host-companion=file:../vitadeck-host-companion-0.1.0.tgz"
   npm install && npm run tsc && npm run host
   ```
   The `npm pkg set` line only stands in for npm publishing.
3. In VitaDeck, press F1 and confirm **Upload**. In a third terminal (same `PATH`), from `/tmp/vdp/lights`, run `npx vitadeck dev <upload URL>`.
4. In VitaDeck, open **Host Control** and run `vitadeck-host-companion link <address>`.
5. Press F1, run **lights**, then press Enter on **Greet**.
6. Edit the message in `host/companion.ts` and save. `vitadeck dev` rebuilds, the companion prints `Reloaded plugins`, and Greet shows the new text.
7. To try the user path:
   1. Stop `npm run host`, then run `vitadeck-host-companion install dist/lights.vdplugin.zip && vitadeck-host-companion start`. Greet still works.
   2. Run `vitadeck-host-companion remove lights`. Greet shows `unknown_plugin`.

Review: https://matemolnar8.github.io/vitadeck/pr/145/

## Review

| Reviewer | Round 1 | Round 2 | Round 3 | Round 4 | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Opus 5.5 (high) | 7/10 | 9/10 | 7/10 | 9/10 | APPROVE |
| Muse Wonder 1.0 (high) | 8/10 | 9/10 | - | - | APPROVE |

Rounds 3 and 4 reviewed the switch from one `.vdplugin` file to the package and zip, which you asked for after rounds 1 and 2.

<details><summary>Review ledger</summary>

| Reviewer | Id | Severity | Outcome | Also raised by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Opus 5.5 | R1 data: URL breaks bundled CommonJS | should | fixed | - |
| Claude Opus 5.5 | R2 INIT_CWD breaks the scaffold's host script | should | fixed | - |
| Claude Opus 5.5 | R3 one broken installed plugin fails start | nit | declined | Muse Wonder 1.0 (R4) |
| Claude Opus 5.5 | R4 slug starting with a digit gives a rejected id | nit | fixed | Muse Wonder 1.0 (R1) |
| Claude Opus 5.5 | R5 root devDependency on the SDK looks unused | nit | disagree | Muse Wonder 1.0 (R5) |
| Claude Opus 5.5 | R6 fs.watch has no error listener | nit | fixed | - |
| Claude Opus 5.5 | R7 module copy written in place | nit | fixed | - |
| Claude Opus 5.5 | R3.1 a broken build deletes the last good package | should | fixed | - |
| Claude Opus 5.5 | R3.2 the zip drops exec bits on scripts | should | fixed (documented: run scripts through their interpreter) | - |
| Claude Opus 5.5 | R3.3 symlinks in files/ are dropped from the zip | nit | fixed | - |
| Claude Opus 5.5 | R3.4 top-level reads of files/ go stale | nit | fixed (documented) | - |
| Claude Opus 5.5 | R3.5 files "." or a file | nit | fixed | - |
| Claude Opus 5.5 | R3.6 --plugin with a .zip | nit | fixed | - |
| Claude Opus 5.5 | R3.7 __MACOSX/ in hand-made zips | nit | fixed | - |
| Claude Opus 5.5 | R4.8 a failed files/ copy leaves a broken package | nit | fixed | - |
| Muse Wonder 1.0 | R1 scaffold builds an id the companion rejects | should | fixed | Claude Opus 5.5 (R4) |
| Muse Wonder 1.0 | R2 command entries not shape-checked | nit | declined | - |
| Muse Wonder 1.0 | R3 built-in id through --plugin exits | nit | declined | - |
| Muse Wonder 1.0 | R4 install not atomic; bad installed file fails start | nit | fixed (atomic install), declined (skip) | Claude Opus 5.5 (R3) |
| Muse Wonder 1.0 | R5 root devDependency on the SDK looks unused | nit | disagree | Claude Opus 5.5 (R5) |
| Muse Wonder 1.0 | R6 id length cap below the slug limit | nit | fixed | - |

R5: the root dependency is what lets the `create --host-plugin` overlay template, which sits outside any workspace package, resolve `@vitadeck/sdk` for the SDK's `tsc` and type-aware lint. Without it, both fail.

</details>

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Custom plugins execute bundled Node code with the installing user's permissions on the LAN computer; the companion loader and SDK build/scaffold contract change for all Host Control authors.
> 
> **Overview**
> Replaces per-plugin npm packages and config-driven companion loading with **built-in** `core` and `systemStats` (registry in `@vitadeck/sdk/host-control`) and **Host Plugin Packages** (`.vdplugin` / `.vdplugin.zip`) that authors build from `hostPlugin` in `vitadeck.config.json`.
> 
> The **`vitadeck` CLI** now builds bundled `companion.mjs` plus optional `files/`, scaffolds with `create --host-plugin` or `--host-plugin-only`, and can run plugin-only `dev` without a Runtime Upload URL. **`implementHostPlugin`** and **`HostCommandError`** move into the SDK so package entries are self-contained.
> 
> **`vitadeck-host-companion`** is a dependency-free rolldown bundle with `start`, `link`, **`install`**, and **`remove`**. It loads packages from `~/.vitadeck/plugins/`, `--plugin` paths, watches for changes, and hot-reloads while keeping the last good set on failure. The separate **`js/host-plugins/`** workspace is removed; the host-control example and Shell link hint point at the new CLI name.
>
